findings.evidence: Write to the requested path; else next to the user's existing deck, else a workspace path such as `slides/<topic>.md`. ... If writing is impossible, return the Markdown inline and never claim a save.
findings.fix: Agents already choose save locations this way. Cut the Save section to the one fact they would miss: use `/mnt/user-data/outputs/` only if it exists, and report whether the deck was rendered or only linted.

findings.evidence: Outline claim, evidence, action toward what the audience must decide or learn. Never reuse a template's sample narrative.
findings.fix: Expand the outline step into a short expert framework: a rough slide budget per talk length (for example about one content slide per 1-2 minutes), where section dividers go, and when to move detail into speaker notes instead of splitting slides.

findings.evidence: casual-slides assertion: "Content headings are concise and slides have at most five bullets each."; expected_output: "suitable technical theme"
findings.fix: Make the assertions in casual-slides checkable: "Every `##` heading is at most 45 characters", "Keeps `theme: default` and the tech template's `<style>` block" and "Contains no `Topic1`/`Point1` placeholders".

findings.evidence: marp --no-stdin deck.md --images png -o /tmp/deck/slide.png    # one PNG per slide, needs a browser
findings.fix: Add the missing branch to Validate: if Marp CLI runs but no browser is found and `--browser-path`/`CHROME_PATH` cannot be set, run the HTML parse check plus the lint list, then tell the user the deck was parsed but not visually checked.
